evidence.exception: Scope is deterministic isolated-module behavior of generateCoda.ts under a closed dependency allowlist (LLM client, search, DB, socialSubjects, claimChecker, usageLog and logger are honest mocks). Whether the raised 400-token ceiling is sufficient for a real Hebrew coda is a live-model outcome and is NOT claimed here; what is proven is that a max_tokens-truncated tool block now returns null with an attributable warn + usage line instead of a silent null. The postReply.ts change is one logger.info line on an existing drop branch (source-traced + typecheck; the harness does not load postReply).

surfaces.reason: Harness default senderRole 'owner' (case 18, 9, 19, 11) plus case 2 owner-authored sibling subjects — owner-recipient compose path exercised before and after.
Case 26 (senderRole 'colleague', language 'he') and cases 1/3/17 exercise the colleague compose path; the new usage/warn lines are role-independent (same code after the create call).

Every harness compose passes channelId 'D_RECIPIENT' (a 1:1 DM), and the transport gate postReply.ts:255-258 only lets a coda through when !isMpim && !isChannel — the DM is the only surface a coda can reach.

Codas never post in a room or MPIM: postReply.ts:255-258 `isOneOnOneDm = !isMpim && !isChannel; if (!isOneOnOneDm) { logger.warn('Social coda suppressed — not a 1:1 DM'); return; }` runs before composeSocialCoda is ever called, so none of the changed lines is reachable from a shared surface.

The change introduces no new remote/unavailable dependency: logLlmUsage (usageLog.ts:38-60) is a synchronous, try/catch'd local log write; the LLM-client-throws branch is unchanged (generateCoda.ts:457-459 catch → warn 'generateSocialCoda threw' → null) and upstream unavailable search/history dependencies remain covered by preserved cases 14/15 (fail-open to the other grounding source, no new warn).
